title: Menachem Talmia
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: At the end of Yerushalmi Sanhedrin, chapter 2, R' Yochanan told R' Yudan Nesia, “Send for Menachem Talmia.” (It appears that Menachem Talmish was a great man, a sage and a scribe; R' Yudan Nesia had asked R' Yochanan about some secret matter, and he answered that he should send for Menachem.) As it is written, “The teaching of kindness is on her tongue.” In Kohelet Rabbah, chapter 5, on “When they increase,” R' Chananiah and R' Yonatan asked Menachem Talmia. R' Berechyah, in R' Yosi bar Ch.’s name, says instead that Menachem Talmia asked them, etc.[^1]

notes.text: The parenthetical reconstruction is Hyman’s conjecture, introduced by “it appears.” טלמיש remains Talmish there, distinct from Talmia elsewhere. The repeated ר״י initials are expanded from the two names immediately preceding; the patronymic בר״ח after Yosi remains bar Ch. The final reports reverse who asked whom, and that contrast is not harmonized. The verse opening ברבות is translated without adding a newly researched verse number. ספ״ב and קה״ר פ״ה conventionally give the end of Sanhedrin chapter 2 and Kohelet Rabbah chapter 5. No primary passage or hidden-matter account was independently verified.

Every abbreviated personal honorific remains R'. Neither the narrative roles nor the name of a region supplies a full title. Hyman’s conjectured exchange is not treated as an independently attested title-bearing quotation, and no global identity is assigned to Menachem or the other figures.
